Festivals · January · Ahafo

Addae Tuntum

Kukuom remembers the Ebirimoro war

Addae Tuntum, also called Akwasidae Tuntum, is the festival of the chiefs and people of Kukuom in the Asunafo area of the Ahafo Region. It remembers the Ebirimoro war between the Sefwi and the Ahafo in the 18th century, and the people renew their loyalty to their chief, with a durbar, drumming and dancing. It is usually held in January.

When
Usually January, sometimes December
Where
Kukuom, Asunafo, Ahafo Region
Kept by
The chiefs and people of Kukuom
Also called
Akwasidae Tuntum
Region
Ahafo

What happens

Kukuom keeps Addae Tuntum.2 It remembers the Ebirimoro war, fought between the Sefwi and the Ahafo in the 18th century, and it is when the people reaffirm their commitment to their chief. There is a durbar of chiefs, people wear traditional dress, there is drumming and dancing, and visitors are welcomed to share food and drink.1

Published accounts of Addae Tuntum are short. If you know the festival, tell us more and we’ll add it.

Good to know if you go

  • Where: Kukuom is in the Asunafo area of the Ahafo Region. See the Ahafo page for places nearby.
  • Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio carries the announcement.
  • Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

Questions people ask

What is the Addae Tuntum festival?

The festival of the chiefs and people of Kukuom in the Ahafo Region, remembering the 18th-century Ebirimoro war between the Sefwi and the Ahafo.

When is Addae Tuntum?

Usually in January, sometimes in December.
